To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The IC50 of magnesium for blocking hippocampal N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA)-receptor-mediated currents varied efold (2.72fold) for approximately every15 mV of the membrane potential in the mid range of membrane potential (between -70 and -50 mV).
the NMDA receptors in hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons are more sensitive to magnesium block during the first 15 days of life.
the sensitivity of hippocampus NMDA receptors from rats of different age groups to Mg2+ block changes with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NMDA receptor function in the development of the hippocampus.
the regulation of the NMDAR by magnesium and glycines during the postnatal development of the rat hippocampus.
the role of the N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA)-type of glutamate receptor in the developing nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the voltage-dependent block of the Xenopus oocyte NMDA receptor is not affected by development but that the sensitivity of this receptor to magnesium is reduced by development.
NMDA receptors in rat hippocampus become progressively less sensitive to Mg2+ blockade during postnatal development.
the sensitivity of hippocampus NMDA receptor to magnesium, glycines and NMDA changes with age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMDA receptors in the developing rat hippocampus are more sensitive to Mg2+ block, and less sensitive to activation by glycine, than in the mature rat hippocampus.
the NMDA receptors from the 1-2 days old rats are more sensitive to Mg2+ than those from the 14-15 days old rats.
the sensitivity of the NMDAR to Mg2+ and glycine increases with age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptors are regulated in a developmentally specific way, which may be critical for their function in the brain.
the sensitivity of hippocampus NMDA receptors is different at different ages and that it is important to consider this in studies of NMDA receptor function in development.
the NMDA receptors in the hippocampus are not fully functional at birth, and that their function develops over the next 2 weeks.
